concepts.def: Base-16, a shorthand for binary (0–9, A–F).
A bit is one binary digit; 8 bits make a byte.
ASCII and Unicode represent text as binary codes.
Images stored as pixels with a colour depth.
Sound sampled at a rate and bit depth to store digitally.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Fundamentals Of Data Representation — a core area of GCSE Computer Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Fundamentals Of Data Representation brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Fundamentals Of Data Representation.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Hexadecimal is often used by programmers because it:
options: Is shorter and easier for humans to read than long binary numbers
Is the only base computers can process
Uses fewer than two symbols
Cannot represent large numbers
A calculation's result needs more bits than are available to store it
A file is saved twice
A loop ends too early
Two variables have the same name
A character set mapping characters to binary codes
A type of sound file
A method of encrypting passwords
A programming language

mcqs.q: Increasing the sample rate of a sound recording will:
options: Improve the audio quality and increase the file size
Reduce the file size and the quality
Have no effect on the file at all
Convert the sound into an image

mcqs.q: Why do computers use binary rather than denary?
options: Yes - hexadecimal can only represent colours.
Binary is used because it is quicker for humans to read.
Hardware can reliably distinguish two states, such as high and low voltage, so two digits give dependable storage and processing.
Binary numbers are shorter than the same values in denary.

mcqs.q: When overflow happens, does the computer just get the right answer with extra digits?
options: Binary numbers are shorter than the same values in denary.
No - the extra carry bit does not fit in the available storage, so the stored result is wrong unless the overflow is detected and handled.
Yes - overflow only changes the sign of the answer to positive.
Yes - the computer automatically grows the storage to fit any result.

mcqs.q: Is hexadecimal a different kind of data from binary?
options: Yes - computers store hex numbers separately from binary numbers.
Yes - hexadecimal can only represent colours.
Yes - overflow only changes the sign of the answer to positive.
No - hex is just a more compact way of writing the same values; every hex digit corresponds exactly to four binary bits.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Binary”?
options: An error that occurs when the result of a calculation is too large to be represented in the number of bits available.
The base-16 system using 0-9 and A-F; one hex digit replaces four binary bits, making long binary values easier for humans to read.
Adding binary numbers column by column with carries; 1 + 1 gives 0 carry 1, just as denary addition carries past 9.
The base-2 number system computers use, with only the digits 0 and 1, because hardware reliably distinguishes two electrical states.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Sample rate”?
options: Adding binary numbers column by column with carries; 1 + 1 gives 0 carry 1, just as denary addition carries past 9.
The base-2 number system computers use, with only the digits 0 and 1, because hardware reliably distinguishes two electrical states.
In digital sound, the number of times per second the analogue wave's height is measured; higher rates give better quality and bigger files.
The base-16 system using 0-9 and A-F; one hex digit replaces four binary bits, making long binary values easier for humans to read.

options: The base-2 number system computers use, with only the digits 0 and 1, because hardware reliably distinguishes two electrical states.
